dedupe_keys.name: life cycle greenhouse gas emissions of shared e scooters in 100 eu cities

description: This study by Ruo Jia and Kun Gao of Chalmers University of Technology (Transportation Research Part D, 2025) estimates the life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions of shared electric scooters across 100 EU cities, because earlier assessments relied on static emission factors and idealised operating assumptions. Coverage: shared e-scooter usage data and electricity-mix generation profiles for 100 cities in the European Union, with comparisons at city and country level and sensitivity tests. Manufacturing, shipping and end of life impose a fixed burden of 115.6 kg CO2-equivalent per scooter; operating data show riding consumes 15.9 Wh per km on average and idle scooters draw 1.5 W. With usage patterns taken from the data, total emission factors range from 30 to 124 g CO2-equivalent per km, mainly set by trip frequency, trip distance and the carbon intensity of electricity. Higher utilisation and cleaner electricity are the main routes to climate-neutral systems. Format and access: an open access journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: results depend on the operator data sampled and on the assumed scooter lifetime. The emission factors can be used to convert simulated micromobility trips into emissions in scenario and policy models. It relates to the East Bronx e-scooter pilot and the BTS bikeshare and e-scooter systems data in the catalogue.
